title: Homo Erectus Adopted a Jungle Lifestyle 200,000 Years Ago - Nautilus
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEvolutionHomo Erectus Adopted a Jungle Lifestyle 200,000 Years AgoIt’s a surprising new chapter in our ancient ancestor’s livesJCBy Jake Currie2:00 PM CST on November 18, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWe like to think of ourselves as the pinnacle of hominin evolution (after all, we went to the moon). But if we’re using “length of time on Earth” as our measuring stick, Homo erectus has us beat cold. First popping up on the scene around 2 million years ago, this particular human ancestor was still traveling the globe a scant 100,000 years ago (along with the brand new Homo sapiens). Now, two studies published today are revealing a new chapter in the species’ life—it’s time roaming the jungles of prehistoric China.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayHomo erectus reached China roughly 1.8 million years ago, but it was thought to have vanished from the region by around 400,000 years ago. Encroaching tropical rainforests—dense, complex, and dangerous habitats for our savanna-born kin—were thought to have played a role in its disappearance. But that might not be true. According to the studies, H. erectus survived, living in the jungles as late as 324,000 and 184,000 years ago. Read more: “We Now Know What Denisovans Looked Like”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
